sentences.text: MR DK MODI(1317) for the PETITIONER(s) No. 1 MR MD MODI(1318) for the PETITIONER(s) No. 1 MRS VD NANAVATI(1206) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 2 MR.J.K.SHAH, APP, (2) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 1 ==============================================================
On this auspicious occasion of Lok Adalat, after successful conciliation, settlement is arrived at in this matter.

Mr. D.K. Modi, learned advocate for the applicant and Mrs. V.D.Nanavati, learned advocate for the respondent No.2, on instructions, have tendered withdrawal/compromise pursis today, duly signed by respective parties.
The same is ordered to be taken on record.

As such, on going through the records, it is noticed that the offence alleged against the applicant-original accused under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is not serious in nature and the punishment or penalty prescribed for such offence is not substantial, and in view of the provisions of Section 51 and 52 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, it is compoundable under Section 69 of the said Act.
In view of the above, this application stands disposed of in terms of the withdrawal/compromise pursis.

The applicant is directed to pay fine of Rs. 25,000/- in the office of the High R/CR.RA/561/2011 ORDER Court Legal Services Committee within a period of four weeks failing which, the matter shall stand revived automatically and the said amount be transmitted to the concerned Municipal Corporation.
However, disposing of this matter will not affect any connected matters arising out of the same, incidental or any other proceedings, filed or to be filed before any other court.
It is also required to be noted that this order will not be treated as precedent in any Vinodkumar Joitaram Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 22 July, 2018
